problem: Embodied agents lack evaluation of cross-lingual generalization in LLM-based navigation planning (e.g., Arabic), and grasping pipelines that rely on deterministic shape estimates are unreliable under severe occlusion.
motivation: Robust embodied systems must handle both linguistic variability at the planning layer and geometric uncertainty at the physical interaction layer. Existing VLN work is almost entirely English, and single partial observations admit multiple incompatible 3D shape hypotheses, making deterministic grasp selection unsafe.
key_idea: Evaluate multilingual (English/Arabic) LLM reasoning for VLN within NavGPT, and use Monte Carlo dropout shape completion with a conservative lower-confidence-bound grasp feasibility criterion (UNCLE-Grasp) to handle occlusion.
insight: Only the abstract is available. It reports that models support structured planning in both English and Arabic, but significant gaps appear from parsing limitations and uneven multilingual reasoning. Uncertainty-aware grasping with abstention improves reliability over deterministic baselines. No specific ablations or numbers are given in the abstract.
method: Multilingual NavGPT evaluation: run large and small LLMs within the NavGPT framework on R2R augmented with Arabic translations of instructions, comparing English vs Arabic
UNCLE-Grasp shape completion: sample multiple 3D shape completions of partially occluded strawberries from a single partial observation via Monte Carlo dropout
Conservative grasp aggregation: aggregate grasp feasibility across sampled shapes using a lower confidence bound criterion, with abstention under high uncertainty
Validation in simulation and real-world robotic harvesting versus deterministic baselines

setting.backbone: Various LLMs/SLMs inside NavGPT (frozen, zero-shot) for navigation; MC-dropout shape completion network for grasping
setting.training_data: none for navigation part (training-free NavGPT with Arabic-translated R2R); grasping shape-completion training data not specified in abstract
setting.observation: Textual descriptions of views for NavGPT (R2R); partial single-view observation for strawberry grasping
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (NavGPT); grasp poses with abstention (UNCLE-Grasp)
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (R2R via NavGPT); unspecified simulator for grasping

results: The abstract reports that modern models support structured planning in both English and Arabic but show significant performance gaps due to parsing limitations and uneven multilingual reasoning. UNCLE-Grasp shows improved robustness, safer abstention and better grasp reliability than deterministic baselines, but no numbers are given.
limitations: Navigation study is evaluation only, with no method to close the multilingual gap
Grasping part is domain-specific (strawberries) and unrelated to navigation
